question: Article 11 TEU obligates the EU institutions to engage in open, transparent and regular dialogue with representative associations in order to enable these stakeholders to express their views, and not the other way around, as appears to have been the case in the Timmermans scandal, in which the Commission instructed NGOs to promote the Commission’s position.

Article 317 TFEU governs the granting of subsidies to support policy objectives and the implementation of EU legislation. The use of EU budgetary resources to influence the colegislators in favour of the European Commission’s position, as came to light in the Timmermans scandal, is not a purpose that can be inferred from Article 317 TFEU. 1.

Does the Commission consider it compatible with Article 11 TEU for NGOs funded by the Commission to promote the Commission’s positions and legislative proposals during a legislative process which is still ongoing?

On what specific legal basis in Article 317 TFEU does the Commission base its subsidisation of NGO activities aimed at influencing Members of the European Parliament on legislative proposals that have not yet been adopted?

Does the Commission share the view that the objective referred to in Article 317 TFEU of improving the implementation of EU legislation relates, by its very nature, to legislation that has already been adopted and entered into force, and not to legislative proposals that are still in the decision-making phase?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.3.2026) The Commission supports stakeholder participation in policy discussions in line with the Treaties and the applicable programme regulations and financial rules. The policy objectives, scope and eligibility conditions of this support is defined in the sectoral basic acts adopted by the European Parliament and the Council.

For example, Article 11 of the Programme for the Environment and Climate Action (LIFE) regulation1, as adopted by the co-legislator, specifically indicates that ‘operating grants shall support the functioning of non-profit making entities which are involved in the development, implementation and enforcement of Union legislation and policy’.

The Commission observes full impartiality and does not require beneficiaries to undertake advocacy activities, nor does it instruct them to support specific positions2. Funding is awarded through transparent and competitive open calls for proposals. Applicants submit proposals describing their work programmes or activities in the areas indicated in the call.

The work programme may mention, among others, applicant’s advocacy activities. Any opinions expressed and activities carried out remain the sole responsibility of the nongovernmental organisations. Civil society entities remain fully autonomous and free to establish their own views on all policy matters.
1 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32021R0783. 2 The Commission guidance on funding for activities (https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-

tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/common/guidance/guidance-funding-dev-impl-monit-enforce-of-eulaw_en.pdf) clarifies that the EU does not require or mandate, as a condition for EU funding, carrying out specifically detailed activities directed at EU institutions or their members.
